How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.

31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses.
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com to help the many people who want to start a business online do so.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

Alex

If you're new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I'm the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It's a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I'll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Open 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything.
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time.
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked.
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months.
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal.
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses.
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com to help the many people who want to start a business online do so.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we're all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win.

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles.

Never quit,

Alex

title: 7 "Unsexy" Businesses That Make You Rich Faster
description:
There's a glitch in your brain right now, and it's costing you six figures over your lifetime. It's called prestige bias, the compulsion to only take a business idea seriously if it sounds impressive at a dinner party. Your brain will let you dump money into a hyped crypto coin with zero due diligence, but mention a vending machine route or a gutter cleaning business, and that same brain instantly dismisses it as beneath you. In this video, we break down seven overlooked businesses, all startable under $5,000, that quietly generate real, trackable monthly cash flow while everyone else chases ideas that sound impressive but produce nothing.

We start by naming the lie underneath the problem: the belief that you need a big, disruptive idea to build real wealth, a belief that's convenient for venture capitalists and media ecosystems that need a hero's journey to sell courses, but useless for actually paying your rent. We break down the exact math behind a vending machine and micro market route, showing how four machines bought for around $4,000 can generate roughly $1,500 a month, and how that scales to $7,500 a month at twenty machines once you hire a part-time route driver and step back from restocking yourself.

This video covers pressure washing, post-construction cleaning contracts, and small-scale mobile fleet and equipment washing, showing exactly how these businesses stack together by sharing equipment, trucks, and client relationships to compound your effective hourly return far beyond a single nine-to-five paycheck. We explain why contractors lose more money from missed deadlines than they save from cheaper cleaning quotes, why pitching on schedule reliability beats pitching on price, and why a simple two-minute check-in text after every job statistically triples referral rates in owner-operator service businesses.

You'll also get a concrete 90-day execution framework: pick the business that made you least uncomfortable, price out real used equipment costs in your specific market, identify three named potential clients before spending a dollar, and track your actual hourly return instead of just total revenue, because a business bringing in $1,200 a month for six hours of work beats one bringing in $2,000 a month for forty. We close with the single filter every quietly wealthy operator on this list actually uses: does this produce more cash than it costs, on a schedule you can rely on.

title: 8 Boring Businesses That Make Money While You Sleep (The Honest Version)
description:
Is there really a business that makes money while you sleep? In this story, a quiet owner stands in a laundromat on Marlowe Avenue on a Sunday evening, watching a man in a Rams jersey feed quarters into dryer nine, while a friend texts screenshots of a dropshipping course. The laundromat, along with a few other businesses nobody connects to him, sent $4,180 to his checking account last month.

This video walks through eight boring, unglamorous businesses, from a $3,200 vending machine to a $210,000 down-payment commercial building. Each one comes with real startup costs, example monthly numbers, and the hidden costs most "passive income" videos skip.

You'll meet the people who run them. Mr. Ostrowski and his dinner-plate key ring teach the first lesson: location is everything. Carol rents out steel shipping containers and explains why the cost hides in the exceptions. Gary runs a self-serve dog wash. Dev learns the hard way that a boring business still needs a reason to stay boring. Ray treats his car wash like a bank that sells soap. Mrs. Delgado sells you a laundromat and one sentence about getting bored. Mr. Whitfield rents people the delay. And Ingrid collects rent from a single pharmacy tenant under a triple net lease.

The video is honest about the word "passive." None of these businesses earns money entirely while you sleep. They turn your attention into a schedule instead of a crisis, and they fail one dryer at a time. It also explains why the more hands-off a business gets, the more it costs to start and the more it punishes one bad assumption.

The eight businesses covered:

Vending machine ($3,200)
Shipping container storage ($6,500)
Self-serve dog wash ($18,000)
Water refill station ($28,000)
Self-serve car wash bay ($60,000 down)
Laundromat ($85,000 down)
Self-storage units ($140,000 down)
Single-tenant commercial building ($210,000 down)

Why boring businesses can beat exciting ones
How cash flow actually works in each business
The hidden costs: repairs, insurance, vacancies and competition
Why a business needs a reason to stay boring
Why "passive income" is usually a business after the problems are solved
How to start small and test before committing big money

title: Three Popular Side Hustles That Are a Waste of Time
description:
Are you worried about pursing an income source that may not lead to any money? Are you fed up with being confused about finding a side hustle that actually brings in money?

Most side hustles and business opportunities just end up taking up your time for very little money. I don't want you to waste your valuable time.

I know what it feels like. I've tested out every side hustle possible over the last decade to see what's worth the time and what is just a waste of time.

I know that you have limited free time and you want to start a side hustle so that you can bring in some extra cash for your debt/bills/savings.

What three popular side hustles are the biggest waste of time going into the 20s? Let’s look at bad side hustles...

Side hustle #1: Driving for a ridesharing company.

When I first worked as a rideshare driver in 2015, I felt that it was a decent side hustle. I found ways to make money by maximizing when I drove.

I'm now here to admit that being a driver for a rideshare company isn't the best use of your time.

Full story here: https://studenomics.com/earning-more/...

Side hustle #2: Flipping stuff.

People think that they're going to find a rare artifact at a yard sale and then flip it for millions. The reality is that you end up with a home filled with crap that nobody else wants.

Side hustle #3: Blogging.

You can turn a blog into a real business. Most of the time, blogging is a fun hobby. Don't expect to turn a quick profit or to get rich from blogging.

I'm not saying that these side hustles are a total waste of time. I just don't want you to think that you can get rich quick from these popular side hustles.

🔹 The biggest mistakes beginners make when evaluating “boring” businesses

💵 THE $70K/MONTH CLAIM — EXPLAINED

You've probably seen headlines claiming that certain “boring businesses” make **$70,000+ per month**.

But here's the question most videos don't ask:

*$70,000 of WHAT?*

Revenue?

Profit?

Owner salary?

Cash flow?

Those numbers can be dramatically different.

That's why this video doesn't simply throw impressive income claims at you.

Instead, we'll look underneath the headline and examine the actual business model.

Because *$100,000 in revenue doesn't mean $100,000 in your pocket.*

Labor, equipment, fuel, rent, insurance, supplies, taxes, marketing, maintenance, debt, and other operating expenses can significantly change the final result.

🧠 THE BIGGER LESSON

The most important lesson isn't:

“Go start a cleaning company.”

It's this:

*Learn to recognize problems people repeatedly pay to have solved.*

Trends change.

Technology changes.

Consumer attention changes.

But people will continue needing essential services.

And businesses built around recurring demand can potentially create something much more valuable than a one-time transaction: *repeat customers and predictable cash flow.*

Watch until the end to discover the characteristics that can turn an ordinary local service into a scalable business.

👋 About This Video

Working a 9-5 doesn’t always cut it when it comes to making ends meet. Sometimes you need extra money and you need it right now. Instead of applying to another job that will take weeks to pay you, try out these jobs that pay cash on the spot.

➡ Craigslist

Whether you’re looking to make extra cash to pay for bills, or just want to save money for your rainy day fund, then Craigslist is a good place to start. The classified ad website offers some of the best side hustle jobs that can be done in your after hours or on days you’re not working your regular job.

If you don’t mind doing minor labor work or household duties, then the ‘services’ section within Craigslist is a good place to search for jobs that pay cash. There you’ll find some of the most random jobs ranging from quick yard work to help moving heavy boxes.

A few years back when I moved into my Boston high rise apartment, I posted a service job on Craigslist for help hanging portraits and frames on the wall. I offered to pay $60 cash on the spot for what I thought would be a couple of hours worth of work. It ended up taking the guy 45 minutes to hang all my artwork. He made out pretty well I would say! 

➡ Scrap Metal

Scrap Metal for money ranks darn close to the top for best paying jobs that pay cash on the spot. If you have a truck and enjoy going on scavenger hunts, then this could be the side hustle job for you.

Driving around and picking up curbside metals found discarded on the street or from trash bins on collection day, can be a lucrative way to spend your free time. 

One good haul of scrap metal to local recycling centers can net you $100 - $500 depending on the metal. 

Here are just some examples of scrap metal you can recycle for cash:

▪ Washers + Dryers
▪ Old plumbing (drains, faucets, pipes and wiring)
▪ Refrigerators + Freezers
▪ Auto Parts
▪ Aluminum Cans

For current national scrap metal prices, a good resource to check is the iScrap app website.

➡ Dog Sitter

It’s estimated that nearly 4 out of 10 households in the U.S. have companion dogs in the home. So there’s a good chance someone in your neighborhood owns dogs and may need dog sitting help at some point or another! 

If you’re great with dogs and love spending time with them, then it may be worthwhile to consider becoming a dog sitter in your area. Your neighbors may also be more open to hiring you if they are familiar with seeing you around the area and know you live close by. 

If you’re curious to know how much to charge, then one quick hack is to call a few local competitors and pose as a customer to get their rates. Once you have a general idea of how much professional pet sitters charge, you can set your rate slightly lower to get your first few clients.

Post some flyers around your area and get ready to get paid to play with your new furry friends!

description:
So I have wondered what my future would be and of course how to make it better. You might have already noticed that most people don’t like to work on their job. They usually say:
“Oh her job has better opportunities.”
“Oh his salary is higher than mine.”

I noticed that the majority of people are saying similar things like that, so it made me wonder, what are the chances that in the future, I might say the same words as well. In other words, in the future, I might not be happy with my job as well.

So ever since childhood, I’ve always wanted the same thing. Happiness. So if I work from 9am to 5pm which is literally the whole day and from Monday to Friday, 5 days a week, which means I only have 2 days to do whatever I want for the whole day. And if I’m not happy with my job, or if I don’t have good relationship with my boss, or if I don’t have good friends in the job who I can have fun with, the majority of my time will be invested in doing something that I’m not happy.

So I thought how do I fix that? How do I make sure that I’ll be happy in the future?
